non_goals: Live traffic or routing data. The estimate uses only what a booking knows, by design.
Fare prediction. Duration is the target; fare is one of the excluded post-trip fields.
risks: One month of data. Seasonality across the year (summer traffic, holidays) is not represented.
Distance is reconstructed per zone pair, so trips inside a large zone share one estimate of distance.
The interval assumes roughly normal residuals; long delays such as accidents are heavier-tailed than that.
lessons: The fields that would make this model look best are exactly the ones a booking cannot know. Excluding them costs score and buys a model that can run.
A lookup table of historical route durations is the right baseline to beat. Beating a global median proves very little.
Target encoding is only safe out-of-fold. Computed in-sample, every row contributes to its own feature.
